scenes.caption: On a cold island at the edge of the North Sea lived a man named Elias. Every night he kept one light burning, so the ships would find their way home.
But Elias himself was lost. Late-night snacks, no movement, and a short temper that pushed away everyone who tried to help him.
One morning, an old sailor left him a note. It said: before you guide others, learn to guide yourself. Start with one empty morning.
So Elias fasted. Sixteen hours, from dinner to noon. The first days were hard, but every time he wanted to quit, he looked at the light and waited.
Within weeks, his mind was clearer than it had been in years. Not because fasting is magic, but because he kept the same window, every single day.
The lighthouse had one hundred and twelve steps. At first, Elias climbed them once and stopped to breathe. So he made a rule: climb them every day.
Then twice a day. Then he added squats at the top and push-ups at the bottom. The workout was never perfect. It was simply never skipped.
Consistency beat intensity. A small workout done daily built a body that a big workout done once a month never could.
The last lesson was the hardest. Elias had to stop the harm. No more drinking to forget, and no more angry words thrown at the people around him.
When anger came, he walked the stairs instead of shouting. When cravings came, he wrote them down and let them pass. Protect yourself, and you protect others too.
One stormy night, a fishing boat lost its engine near the rocks. Elias ran down all one hundred and twelve steps without stopping, and pulled the crew to safety.
Fast with a fixed window. Train a little, every day. Stay away from harm against yourself and others. That is the system. This is Alpha Talks 3000, and the light is yours to keep.
